title: Expression and purification of tag-free SARS-CoV-2 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase in Escherichia coli
protocol: Inoculate a single colony from the plate containing E. coli BL21/pcIts,ind+(NSP8) into 8 mL of Terrific broth with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Incubate for 16 h with shaking at 30°C, 200 rpm.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 5,000 × g for 10 min.
Decant the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 6 mL of fresh Terrific broth with 100 μg/mL ampicillin.
Inoculate each of 2 × 1 L of Terrific broth with 100 μg/mL ampicillin, split into 2 × 2.8 L baffle-bottomed flasks, with 3 mL of the resuspended culture from step 3.
Incubate the culture at 30°C with shaking at 250 rpm.
Measure the OD600 of the culture every 30 min until the OD600 reaches 2.
Remove a “pre-induction” sample by pelleting (10,000 × g, 5 min, 20°C–25°C) a volume of cells equal to 1 mL at an OD600 of 6.
Aspirate the supernatant then store the pellet at −80°C.
Induce expression by moving the cultures to an incubator preheated to 42°C for 20 min and incubate with shaking at 250 rpm.
Move the cultures to an incubator preheated to 38°C and incubate with shaking at 250 rpm for 3 h.
Measure the OD600 of the cultures.
Take a post-induction sample by pelleting a volume of cells equal to 1 mL at an OD600 of 6.
Decant then aspirate the remaining supernatant.
Store the pellet at -80°C.
Harvest the cells by centrifugation at 6,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant.
Transfer the pellet to a pre-weighed 50 mL conical tube with a spatula.
Determine the mass of the tube plus pellet then subtract the mass of the empty tube to get the yield of cell pellet.
Record the mass on the tube as well as in your notes.
Store the pellet at -80°C.
Inoculate the starter culture into 1 L of Terrific broth containing 30 μg/mL kanamycin and 20 μg/mL chloramphenicol in a 2.8 L baffle-bottomed flask.
Incubate with shaking at 30°C, 250 rpm.
Periodically check the OD600 of the culture.
Harvest a volume of cells equal to 1 mL when the OD600 reaches 6 and store the pellet at −80°C as a pre-induction sample.
Add tetracycline from a 10 μg/mL stock to achieve a final concentration of 10 ng/mL in the culture.
Move the culture to an incubator cooled to 16°C.
Incubate with shaking at 16°C, 250 rpm for 20 min.
Add IPTG to 0.5 mM from a 1 M stock solution.
Make fresh daily a 25 mg/mL nalidixic acid stock by dissolving the powder into 0.3 M NaOH.
Add nalidixic acid to 50 μg/mL from a freshly made 25 mg/mL stock.
Incubate with shaking at 16°C, 250 rpm for 16 h.
Measure the OD600 of the culture after expression.
Pellet a volume of cells equal to 1 mL when the OD600 reaches 6 and store the pellet at −80°C.
Centrifuge the cells at 6,000 × g for 20 min at 4°C to harvest them.
Decant the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Transfer the cell pellet to a pre-weighed 50 mL conical tube with a spatula.
Determine the mass of the harvested pellet and store it at −80°C.
Thaw pellets collected pre- and post-induction from large-scale expressions on ice.
Add 200 μL of Expression Test Buffer A containing 0.3 mg/mL Lysozyme to each pellet.
Vortex until the pellets have been uniformly resuspended.
Incubate samples at 37°C for 10 min then place on ice.
Sonicate with the micro-tip (20% duty cycle, 0% output) for 30 – 40 bursts.
Add 22.4 μL of 5 M NaCl to each sample.
Seal the tubes and vortex.
Remove 15 μL of the sonicate and transfer it to the appropriate “TCP” sample tube containing 45 μL of Expression Test Sample Buffer.
Spin the remainder of the sonicate in a microcentrifuge tube at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Remove 15 μL of the supernatant and transfer to an appropriate “SOL” sample tube containing Expression Test Sample Buffer.
Aspirate off the remaining supernatant.
Add 400 μL of Expression Test Buffer B and resuspend the pellet using sonication.
Spin the suspension at 16,000 × g for 10 min at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Add 192 μL of Expression Test Buffer B to each sample and resuspend the pellets by sonication.
Remove 15 μL of the resuspended pellet solution and transfer to an appropriate “INS” tube containing Expression Test Sample Buffer.
Heat all samples at 80°C–85°C for 5 min prior to loading for SDS-PAGE.
Load 10 – 15 μL per lane for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Thaw the bacterial pellet on ice.
Resuspend the cell pellet in Lysis Buffer-1 at 5 mL buffer per gram of E. coli.
Add 800 mM phenylmethylsulfonyl fluoride (PMSF) to achieve a final concentration of 10 mM.
Add 30 mg/mL Lysozyme to obtain a final concentration of 0.3 mg/mL and stir at 25°C for 15 minutes on a stir plate.
Sonicate the lysate at 20% duty with power 5 on ice for 20 minutes, stirring constantly.
Check the sample every 3-5 minutes during sonication to ensure efficient mixing and cooling.
Add 4% sodium deoxycholate to achieve a final concentration of 0.1%.
Add 5 M NaCl to obtain a final concentration of 0.5 M.
Stir on ice for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge the lysate at 75,000 × g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Filter the supernatants through a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Measure the conductivity of Buffer A-1 containing 10% Buffer B-1.
Dilute the filtered sample with Dilution Buffer-1 until its conductivity matches that of Buffer A-1 with 10% Buffer B-1 (approximately a 5-fold dilution).
Remove an aliquot of the diluted sample into 6× SDS Sample Buffer for later analysis by SDS-PAGE.
Flow the lysate onto two sequential 5 mL HiTrap Q FF columns, equilibrated in Buffer A-1, at 10 mL/min with the outlet connected to two sequential 5 mL HiTrap SP-FF columns.
Monitor absorbance at 280 nm during flow-through collection.
Collect and store the flow-through in a separate container labeled for storage at 4°C.
Wash with 10% Buffer B-1 until the UV 280 reaches baseline (approximately 100 mL).
Collect the eluate in a separate container.
Save a sample for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Store the collected eluate at 4°C.
Disconnect the Q columns, leaving the two SP columns connected to the FPLC.
Elute proteins bound to the SP column with a 200 mL gradient from 10%–80% Buffer B at 5 mL/min.
Collect 5 mL fractions and store on ice.
Remove aliquots of various fractions with a large A280 peak in the chromatogram into 6× SDS Sample Buffer.
Heat samples at 85°C for 5 min.
Load samples onto 15% SDS-PAGE gels.
Run the gel until the bromophenol blue reaches the bottom of the gel following the manufacturers protocol.
Stain and destain the gel with Coomassie brilliant blue.
Pool fractions containing nsp8.
Pause point: Fractions can be left at 4°C for up to 16 hours.
Dilute the pooled fractions with Dilution Buffer-1 until the conductivity of the sample is equal to the conductivity of Buffer A-1.
Load the diluted sample onto a 5 mL HiTrap Blue-HP column, equilibrated in Buffer A-1 at 10 mL/min.
Collect the flow through in a separate, labeled container.
Save a sample for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Store the collected flow-through at 4°C.
Wash the column with 10% Buffer B at 5 mL/min until the UV280 reaches baseline.
Collect and save a sample of the eluate for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Store the collected eluate at 4°C.
Elute bound proteins with a 50 mL linear gradient from 10% to 80% Buffer B at 5 mL/min, collecting 2 mL fractions.
Analyze samples from the Blue column by SDS-PAGE as described above.
Pool fractions containing nsp8.

Concentrate the pooled fractions by ultrafiltration with Amicon Ultra centrifugal concentrators with a 10 kDa molecular weight cutoff (MWCO) at 4°C until the sample volume is less than 1 mL, following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Inject the sample onto the Superdex 200 10/300 GL column, equilibrated in 10% Buffer B with the sample loop on the HPLC.
Elute proteins with 10% Buffer B-1, collecting 1 mL fractions.
Analyze fractions by SDS-PAGE as described above.
Pool fractions containing nsp8.
Determine the concentration of nsp8 by absorbance at 280 nm using the extinction coefficient ε280: 19,940 M−1 cm−1.
Concentrate the sample with Amicon Ultra centrifugal concentrators (10 kDa MWCO) if necessary, following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Dialyze the sample into Storage Buffer-1 with 1 kDa MWCO dialysis tubing at 4°C with 2 × 500 mL × 1 h buffer changes.
Thaw cells from previous expression and resuspend in Lysis Buffer-2 at 5 mL buffer per gram of E. coli cells.
Dissolve one EDTA-free protease inhibitor tablet into 2 mL of Lysis Buffer-2 and add to the sample for each 50 mL of lysis buffer used.
Add 800 mM PMSF to a final concentration of 10 mM in the lysate.
Add 4% sodium deoxycholate to a final concentration of 0.1% in the lysate.
Add 30 mg/mL lysozyme to a final concentration of 0.3 mg/mL in the lysate.
Stir at 25°C for 15 min on a stir plate.
Sonicate the lysate on ice for 20 min with stirring (20% duty cycle, power 5).
Check ice cooling every 5 min during sonication.
Clarify the lysate by centrifugation at 75,000 × g at 4°C for 1 hour.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Measure the conductivity of Buffer A-2.
Measure the conductivity of the sample and dilute with Dilution Buffer-2 until the conductivity is equal to that of Buffer A-2 (~6 fold dilution).
Load the sample at 5 mL/min onto a 30 mL Q Sepharose-FF column equilibrated in Buffer A-2.
Collect and store the flow through at 4°C.
Wash with Buffer A until the UV reaches baseline, collecting the eluate in a separate container and storing it at 4°C.
Elute bound proteins with a 300 mL linear gradient from 0%–100% Buffer B-2, collecting 10 mL fractions.
Filter the pooled fractions containing nsp12/7/8 with a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Dilute the filtered fractions with Dilution Buffer-2 until the conductivity is equal to that of Buffer A-2.
Load the diluted sample onto a HiTrap Blue-HP column at 5 mL/min and collect the flow through, containing nsp12/7/8.
Store the collected flow through from the blue column at 4°C before proceeding.
Load this flow through directly on to a 5 mL Heparin Sepharose 6-FF column equilibrated in Buffer A-2 at 5 mL/min and collect the flow through in a separate labeled container, storing it at 4°C.
Wash with Buffer A-2 until the UV reaches baseline, collecting the eluate in a separate labeled container and storing it at 4°C.
Elute bound proteins with a 50 mL linear gradient of 0%–100% Buffer B-2 at 2.5 mL/min, collecting 5 mL fractions.
Analyze results by SDS-PAGE as described above.
Pool fractions containing nsp12/7/8 complex.
Filter pooled fractions using a 0.2 μm syringe filter.
Dilute filtered fractions with Dilution Buffer-2 to match the conductivity of Buffer A-2.
Load diluted sample onto a 5 mL HiTrap SP-FF column at 5 mL/min, collecting flow through on ice.
Concentrate flow through from the SP column using Amicon Ultra centrifugal concentrators (30 kDa MWCO) until volume is less than 0.5 mL.
Inject concentrated sample onto a Superdex 200 10/300 GL column equilibrated in Buffer A-2 at 0.75 mL/min.
Collect 1.5 mL fractions during size exclusion chromatography.
Analyze collected fractions by SDS-PAGE.
Pool fractions containing nsp12/7/8 complex.
Concentrate pooled fractions using Amicon Ultra (30 kDa MWCO) centrifugal concentrators until volume is approximately 1 mL.
Dialyze concentrated sample into Storage Buffer-2 with 1 kDa MWCO dialysis tubing at 4°C, changing buffer twice for one hour each.
Remove sample from dialysis tubing.
Determine the final volume of the sample.
Measure the concentration by absorbance at 280 nm using an extinction coefficient of 181,300 M−1 cm−1.
Flash freeze aliquots in liquid nitrogen.
Store frozen aliquots at −80°C.
